hypotheses.statement: Stronger liquidation frictions are expected to increase unresolved debt, bad debt and the magnitude or duration of negative peg deviations.
hypotheses.title: Liquidation frictions

hypotheses.statement: Oracle delay is expected to widen the mismatch between market conditions and protocol action, especially after rapid collateral-price shocks.
hypotheses.title: Oracle delay

hypotheses.statement: Multi-collateral diversification is expected to reduce system losses under isolated collateral-specific shocks, but its benefits should diminish under correlated stress and may reverse when a collateral intended to provide stability experiences its own depeg or liquidity impairment.
hypotheses.title: Diversification and contagion

hypotheses.statement: Recovery is expected to depend jointly on collateral-price rebound, liquidation resolution and behavioural stabilisation, with unresolved backlog limiting the effect of otherwise favourable recovery conditions.
hypotheses.title: Recovery and behavioural stabilisation

purpose: Result-blind pre-registration of the final dissertation experiment programme.

research_questions.text: How do collateral-price shocks propagate through vault collateralisation, liquidation eligibility, keeper execution and DAI price adjustment in the ETH-only core model?
How do gas costs, keeper participation, liquidation capacity and oracle delay affect liquidation completion, bad debt and DAI peg recovery?
Which collateral-recovery and behavioural assumptions materially affect the speed and reliability of peg restoration after stress?
Under what collateral compositions and shock structures does multi-collateral DAI become more resilient than an ETH-only system, and when does diversification instead transmit or concentrate risk?
